name: Goga
classification_notes: Described by the foundry as combining geometric sans and neo-grotesque influences, citing Avenir and Helvetica as inspirations; sits squarely in the grotesque category with geometric leanings.
summary: A nine-weight grotesque family blending geometric and neo-grotesque influences, named after its distinctive alternate lowercase g forms.
description: Goga draws on Avenir and Helvetica to produce a neutral, large x-height grotesque suited to both display and text setting. Nine weights from Thin to Black come with matching italics, and the family ships as a variable font with axes for weight and slant. The stylistic alternate lowercase g forms are the one point of character in an otherwise general-purpose offering.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Goga as a versatile sans serif combining the best of geometric sans serifs and neo-grotesques, inspired by Avenir and Helvetica. Despite its universal, neutral character it carries a warm, friendly spirit, with unusual stylistic alternates for the lowercase g adding personality. The family supports Latin-extended languages, includes a broad set of OpenType features, and is available as a variable font with slant and weight axes.

name: Emilio
classification_notes: Emilio draws from old-style serif models such as Times and Garamond, with calligraphic details and a high x-height that place it in the humanist old-style tradition, updated with reductive modern elements.
summary: A 14-style old-style serif with calligraphic details and an eighties advertising flavour, suited to editorial and branding work.
description: Taking cues from the advertising serifs of the 1980s, particularly Times and Garamond, Emilio introduces modern touches such as reductive calligraphic stroke endings and distinctive K and R leg forms. Seven weights from Thin to Black each carry a matching italic, and a variable font is included in the bundle. A large x-height and modest contrast keep it readable at small sizes, while the display weights are the clearest expression of its character.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Emilio as a modern serif family of 14 styles that balances traditional and modern approaches. Inspired by eighties advertising visuals and typefaces like Times and Garamond, it introduces contemporary details including calligraphy-inspired reductive strokes and distinctive leg shapes on the K and R. Stylistic alternates, standard and discretionary ligatures, and other OpenType features are included, with the foundry positioning it for editorial design, posters, covers, branding and logo design.

name: Azurio
classification_notes: Modern serif with geometric and triangular construction inspired by the mineral Azurite. Pointed wedge serifs, squared counters and triangular crossbar alternates on A and H give it a crisp, hard-edged character. Large x-height and moderate contrast make it viable for text as well as display. Includes stylistic alternates, standard and discretionary ligatures, plus a variable font.
summary: A six-weight sharp serif with mineral-inspired geometry — pointed wedge serifs, squared counters and triangular crossbar alternates give it strong personality at headline sizes.
description: Azurio takes its name and structure from Azurite, translating the mineral's crystalline geometry into a modern serif: pointed wedge serifs, squared counters and optional triangular crossbars on A and H. Six weights from Light to Black are available as static files and a variable font. Despite its display personality, a large x-height and moderate contrast keep it workable for longer text.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Azurio as 'a modern, sharp serif type family ranging from light to black' with 'numerous geometric and triangular details reminiscent of the mineral Azurite', including 'squared counters and pointed wedge serifs'. Stylistic alternates on A and H offer two triangular crossbar variants; the family includes standard and discretionary ligatures and additional OpenType features. Positioned for branding, visual identities, logo design, print and editorial.

name: Banter Grotesk
classification_notes: A display grotesque with deliberately inverted proportions — capitals and numerals are top-heavy, reversing the conventional optical correction. Angled terminals and 11 stylistic sets push it toward the expressive end of the sans spectrum. Variable weight and slant axes.
summary: A 12-style grotesque with deliberately top-heavy proportions and angled terminals — 11 stylistic sets let it shift from playful to punchy.
description: Banter Grotesk inverts the usual optical corrections: capitals and numerals are heavier at the top than the bottom, creating a subtle built-in tension. Angled terminals and 11 stylistic sets — including an 'edgy' set that sharpens the character considerably — give it a range from approachable to confrontational. The family ships as a variable font with weight and slant axes, 650+ characters, circled numerals, fractions and ligatures.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Banter Grotesk as 'a playful and quirky sans serif font family' whose 'proportions break the traditional rules of symmetry, flipping them upside down', particularly evident in capitals and numbers where 'the tops of the letters often outweigh the bottoms'. Variable weight and slant, over 650 characters, 11 stylistic sets and OpenType features including circled numerals and ligatures.

name: Crake
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif with flared serifs and organic detailing. Rounded counters on several uppercase letters are an unusual feature. Five weights from Light to Bold; large x-height with no italic. Nature-inspired.
summary: A five-weight high-contrast display serif fusing organic nature-inspired details with geometric shapes — rounded uppercase counters are its signature quirk.
description: Crake pairs high stroke contrast and flared serifs with organic details drawn from nature, most noticeably the rounded counters on several uppercase letters that soften its otherwise geometric structure. Five weights from Light to Bold cover display and headline use; stylistic alternates let you dial back the expressiveness toward something more conventional. Ligatures and a large x-height round out the feature set.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Crake as 'a contemporary, high-contrast serif typeface with a distinctive look that combines organic, nature-inspired details with geometrical shapes', with 'rounded counters of many uppercase letters' making it 'even more expressive'. Flared serifs, a large x-height, stylistic alternates and discretionary and standard ligatures. Positioned for branding, editorial, magazines and logo design.

name: Girona
classification_notes: A high-contrast sans with prominent inktraps — a marker of contemporary display type design. Five weights, large x-height, no italic. Inktrap detailing and stylistic alternates give it a dual personality between clean and expressive.
summary: A five-weight high-contrast sans with large inktraps and playful details — stylistic alternates shift it between clean-cut and expressive.
description: Girona's defining feature is its prominent inktraps, which give the letterforms a crisp, contemporary character at display sizes. Stroke contrast is high for a sans, and the five-weight range from Light to Bold is complemented by stylistic alternates that let you choose between a delicate, refined look and something more assertive. A large x-height and standard/discretionary ligatures make it a reasonable all-rounder for branding, editorial and logo work.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Girona as 'an elegant, contrasting sans serif typeface available in five weights from light to bold' with 'large inktraps and many playful details' creating 'a modern typeface with a distinctive look'. Stylistic alternates offer 'a clean and delicate' or 'more expressive look', with standard and discretionary ligatures. Positioned for branding, editorial, logo and social media.

name: Goga Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced extension of Goga, rebalanced for a 630-unit grid. Shares the same vertical metrics as Goga for mixed-family layouts. 18 styles from Thin to Black with matching italics. Variable font with weight and slant axes.
summary: An 18-style monospaced companion to Goga, rebalanced to a 630-unit grid — shares vertical metrics with Goga for seamless mixed-family layouts.
description: Goga Mono carries the neo-grotesque warmth of Goga into a true monospaced structure, rebalancing each glyph into a 630-unit system — wide letters compressed, narrow ones widened. Nine weights from Thin to Black with matching italics, plus a variable font covering weight and slant. Signature Goga alternates are retained alongside new options such as a slashed zero and simplified r. Shared vertical metrics mean the two families can be mixed in a layout without adjustment.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Goga Mono as 'a contemporary monospaced extension of the popular Goga family, designed to perform equally well in code and in design-driven contexts', with 'every glyph carefully rebalanced' into a '630-unit system'. Retains Goga's signature alternates and adds slashed zero and simplified r. Shares vertical metrics with Goga. Extended Latin, contextual alternates, case-sensitive forms, circled numbers, fractions and more.

name: Lakovar Sans
classification_notes: A wide-proportioned humanist sans derived from lettering on a historic LAKOVAR sign in Plzeň, Czech Republic. Wide proportions and open counters give it a monumental quality. 7 styles plus a variable font. Primarily display but legible at larger text sizes.
summary: A seven-weight humanist sans with monumental wide proportions, derived from historic Czech sign lettering — confident presence with approachable warmth.
description: Lakovar Sans takes its starting point from the lettering on a historic LAKOVAR sign in Plzeň, Czech Republic, reinterpreting the original forms through a contemporary humanist lens rather than reviving them directly. Wide proportions, open counters and subtle humanist details give it a monumental presence while keeping it approachable and readable. Seven weights from Thin to Black are available as a variable font. Stylistic alternates, ligatures, tabular figures and arrows extend its utility across branding, signage, editorial and digital products.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Lakovar Sans as a typeface that 'began with a single word', inspired by 'the lettering of a historic LAKOVAR sign on a building in Plzeň, Czechia', reinterpreting the originals 'through a modern lens — preserving their distinctiveness, warmth, and spirit'. Wide proportions, open counters and humanist details create 'a confident, monumental presence that remains approachable and highly legible'.

name: Magnete Sans
classification_notes: A multi-width condensed grotesque rooted in early 20th-century grotesks Aurora and Inserat-Grotesk. Four widths (Ultra Narrow, Narrow, Standard, Expanded) × 6 weights = 24 styles. Extensive stylistic alternate system covering leg forms, terminal angles and diagonal directions.
summary: A 24-style multi-width grotesque spanning Ultra Narrow to Expanded — rooted in early 20th-century Aurora and Inserat-Grotesk with extensive stylistic alternates.
description: Magnete Sans spans four widths — Ultra Narrow, Narrow, Standard and Expanded — across six weights from ExtraLight to Bold, yielding 24 styles. The reference points are early 20th-century grotesks Aurora and Inserat-Grotesk, reinterpreted with contemporary refinement. The name nods to the magnetosphere and the Aurora Borealis. Stylistic alternates cover leg forms on k, K and R (vertical, curved or diagonal), terminal angles on t and diagonal directions on vwxy and AMNVWXY — enabling shifts from strict and bold to fluid and soft. Old-style and tabular figures, fractions, case-sensitive forms and Latin Extended complete the feature set.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Magnete Sans as 'a bold and flexible condensed sans serif family available in 4 widths — Ultra Narrow, Narrow, Standard, and Expanded — with 6 weights each, from Extralight to Bold, totaling 24 styles', rooted in 'early 20th-century grotesks like Aurora and Inserat-Grotesk'. Extensive stylistic alternates for leg forms, terminals and diagonals. Old-style and tabular figures, fractions and case-sensitive forms.

name: Neolit
classification_notes: A transitional serif with old-style inflection — Translation contrast (stroke axis angled as in old-style forms) tempers an otherwise transitional structure. Drop terminals, tense curves and a subtly condensed structure add contemporary character. 12 styles from Regular to ExtraBold with true italics. Dual text and display intent.
summary: A 12-style transitional serif with drop terminals, tense curves and an old-style stroke axis — readable in text, sculptural at display sizes.
description: Neolit takes a transitional skeleton and inflects it with old-style Translation contrast — a canted stroke axis that adds movement and a raw, material quality to otherwise polished letterforms. Drop terminals and tense curves bring a contemporary decisiveness. Twelve styles from Regular to ExtraBold each carry a true italic; an extended Latin character set includes circled and squared numerals, fractions, case-sensitive forms and contextual alternates. Performs steadily at text sizes and reveals its sculptural precision at display scales.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Neolit as having 'a transitional backbone tempered by a deliberate use of Translation contrast, a quiet nod to old-style serif forms', with 'decisive features like sturdy drop terminals, tense curves, and a subtly condensed structure'. Conceived with 'an image in mind: a stone, polished by time, but with a strong presence'. 12 styles with true italics, extended Latin, circled and squared numerals, fractions, case-sensitive forms and contextual alternates.

name: Regonia
classification_notes: A Didone-style high-contrast serif referencing Didot and Bodoni. Thin hairlines and curvy details. Single weight, display-only, large x-height. Fancy ligatures and stylistic variations.
summary: A single-weight Didone display serif in the Didot/Bodoni tradition — hairline contrast, curvy details and fancy ligatures for fashion and editorial use.
description: Regonia sits squarely in the Didone tradition, citing Didot and Bodoni as its reference points. Extreme stroke contrast between thin hairlines and thick stems is softened by curvy details that push it away from pure classical severity. A single regular weight focuses it firmly on display and headline use, where a large x-height and fancy ligatures let it carry editorial and fashion contexts with ease. Stylistic variations extend the expressive range.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Regonia as 'a high-contrast display serif typeface inspired by neoclassical typefaces like Didot or Bodoni', with 'thin hairlines and unique curvy details' making it 'an elegant and modern typeface'. Positioned for editorial design, branding, wedding invitations and fashion magazines, with fancy ligatures and stylistic variations.

name: Remixa
classification_notes: A modern sans-serif with serif-inspired detailing and high contrast, positioning it between a pure grotesque and a glyphic display face. The large x-height and display orientation reinforce its contemporary sans classification.
summary: A high-contrast display sans with subtle serif-derived details across six weights, aimed at branding and editorial use.
description: Six weights from Light to Black give Remixa a broad tonal range for headline and display work. Serif-inspired details and visible stroke contrast distinguish it from a plain grotesque, while a generous x-height keeps it legible at large sizes. OpenType features include standard and discretionary ligatures and stylistic alternates, making it a reasonable choice for magazine layouts, brand identities and logo work.
foundry_blurb: Narrow Type describe Remixa as a modern sans-serif that incorporates serif-inspired elements to create a contrasting display family. Six weights from Light to Black support versatile use across branding, logo design, editorial and magazine projects, with OpenType features including ligatures and stylistic alternates throughout.
